To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the use of a combination of speech and visual information is beneficial for event retrieval; (2) the use of concept-based querying in addition to content-based querying is beneficial for event detection; (3) a semi-automatic approach to event modeling is beneficial; (4) a combination of content- and concept-based querying is beneficial; (5) speech is beneficial for event and object retrieval, especially in combination with visual information; and (6) the combination of speech and concept-based querying

(a) a combination of speech and video content-based retrieval can improve retrieval effectiveness; (b) speech and video content can be combined in a unified retrieval system; and (c) speech can improve the effectiveness of video content retrieval.
The proposed approach is able to retrieve events from a database of 1,500 videos, using only 100 videos for training.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a multi-modal system for semantic video retrieval.
developing and applying methods for the detection of events, objects, actions, and other semantic video concepts.
the automatic detection, indexing and retrieval of semantic video content.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the approach has been successful in the detection of semantic events and objects in video and the retrieval of semantic events from video, although there is still room for improvement.
the approach is promising but still needs to be refined and improved.

we are still far from the goal of a fully automatic and reliable system for video event retrieval, and that the best approach is to combine the efforts of the different communities involved, and to use a variety of techniques, including speech retrieval.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we were able to achieve the best overall performance in the TREC Video 2001 Search Track.
the system is able to detect a variety of events and concepts in video, and is capable of retrieving them using both content-based and concept based queries.

we have shown that a combination of speech and video retrieval can be used to improve retrieval performance, and we have also demonstrated that the use of semantic video event retrieval can be used as a means of improving the performance of a speech retrieval system.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a multi-modal approach to video retrieval, where both visual and audio features are used, provides significant improvements in the retrieval performance.
the combination of content-based and text-based search is a powerful tool to improve search results in video retrieval.
the combination of content-based and semantic-based retrieval can provide significant gains in the performance of a multi-modal search engine.
